_meta.note: V2.2 (2026-09-07): two more grounding fixes on top of V2.1. (1) Questions/scripts about how a diagnosis was reached were naming specific ALTERNATIVE components/causes/tests the visitor never supplied ('what ruled out the evaporator fan, damper, or defrost system?') - puts a model-generated hypothesis in the visitor's mouth, making them sound as if they'd already diagnosed the equipment. Fixed: ask neutrally ('what testing led to this diagnosis?'), never name an alternative unless the visitor/quote introduced it - a new 'does this question contain technical knowledge that came from me rather than the visitor or quote?' test runs before questions_to_ask/what_to_say are finalized. (2) Warranty mentions implied another failure is likely/coming rather than describing financial exposure - fixed to frame warranty strictly as exposure ('affects how much financial exposure you retain if a covered problem occurs afterward'), never as a hint of impending failure. New guard prohibitions: alternative_diagnosis_named_for_visitor, warranty_implies_impending_failure. NOTE (unrelated to this fix, worth tracking separately): an operator-side Anthropic credit exhaustion caused 'Analysis failed' in production between the V2.1 and V2.2 fixes - confirmed as a billing issue (400 'credit balance too low'), not a code/prompt bug, and resolved by the account owner topping up credits. The guard's near-universal repair-trigger rate observed during this session's testing is a real, separate cost/latency concern flagged to the owner but not yet addressed - each triggered repair roughly triples the cost of a call.

input.whatWentWrong: Not cooling properly, freezer is fine but the fridge side is warm
input.whatTheyToldYou: Technician said the compressor is failing and needs full replacement

output.understanding: Your 6-year-old Whirlpool refrigerator is cooling on the freezer side but not the fridge side, and a technician has diagnosed a failing compressor and quoted $450 total to replace it. No itemized breakdown or document was provided.
output.verdict_explanation: The $450 figure is a single number with no visible breakdown into parts, labor, or warranty terms. For a compressor replacement on a refrigerator, understanding what that $450 covers — parts, labor, any fees, and whether a warranty is included — is important before approving the work. Separately, the symptom you described (freezer fine, fridge side warm) can have more than one cause, so it is worth understanding what inspection or testing led to the compressor diagnosis specifically.
unknowns_that_matter: What inspection or testing confirmed the compressor as the cause — this matters because the symptom alone (warm fridge side, working freezer) does not uniquely identify one component.
How the $450 breaks down between the compressor part itself and labor — this affects whether the quote is evaluable and comparable to any second quote.
Whether a warranty is included on the part, the labor, or both, and for how long — this affects your financial exposure if a problem recurs.
Whether the compressor part is new or remanufactured, and the brand or specification — this matters for comparing the quote to any alternative.

repair_vs_replace.assessment: A compressor replacement is a significant repair cost. Whether to repair or replace depends on the cost of a comparable new refrigerator and the condition and repair history of this one. Knowing the full breakdown of the $450 quote will help you compare it to replacement options.
missing_information: Current price of a comparable replacement refrigerator
Reliability and repair history of this specific unit
Whether any manufacturer or extended warranty is still in effect

questions_to_ask: Can you break down the $450 into the cost of the compressor part and the labor charge separately?
What specific testing or inspection led to the compressor diagnosis?
What warranty comes with this repair, and does it cover both parts and labor?
Is the compressor part new or remanufactured, and what brand or specification will be used?
output.what_to_say: Before I approve this, I have a few questions. Can you break the $450 into parts and labor, and tell me what the compressor part is — new or remanufactured, and which brand? I also want to understand what testing pointed to the compressor specifically. And what warranty would cover this repair if the problem comes back?

second_opinion.reason: The diagnosis involves a major component and a significant cost. A second opinion could independently assess the cause and confirm whether the repair approach and price are sound.

input.whatTheyToldYou: They said I need new brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels

output.understanding: You have a 2018 Honda Civic with 85,000 miles making a grinding noise when braking, and a shop quoted you $1,800 to replace brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels. No itemized breakdown or document was provided, so the quote is currently a single total with a general scope description.
output.verdict_explanation: The $1,800 total covers a broad scope — pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels — but without any itemization you cannot see what portion is parts, what portion is labor, or what each axle costs separately. Caliper replacement is a significant addition to a standard brake job, and it is worth understanding what inspection or finding led to recommending all four calipers rather than pads and rotors alone. You need more detail before you can meaningfully evaluate or compare this quote.

quote_summary.stated_diagnosis: Grinding noise when braking requires new brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels
quote_summary.proposed_work: Replace brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels

unknowns_that_matter: Whether the calipers truly need replacement on all four wheels is not explained in the quote — the shop has not documented what they found during inspection that led to this recommendation
No itemization is provided, so you cannot see the parts cost, labor cost, or per-axle breakdown within the $1,800 total
Whether the parts are OEM, aftermarket, or remanufactured is not stated, which affects what you would be comparing if you get a second quote
No warranty terms are stated for either parts or labor
questions_to_ask: Can you give me a written breakdown showing parts cost and labor cost separately, and what each axle costs?
What did you observe during inspection that led to recommending caliper replacement on all four wheels?
Are the parts you are quoting OEM, aftermarket, or remanufactured, and what warranty comes with the parts and labor?
Is the diagnostic fee, if any, included in the $1,800 or charged separately?
output.what_to_say: Before I approve the work, I would like a written itemization showing parts and labor separately, and the cost broken down by axle. I also want to understand what the inspection found that points to caliper replacement on all four wheels — can you walk me through that? Finally, what warranty comes with the parts and labor on this job?

second_opinion.reason: Caliper replacement on all four wheels is a significant addition to a standard pad and rotor job. A second shop's independent inspection would help you confirm the scope before committing to the full cost.

output.safety_note: A grinding noise when braking can indicate significantly worn brake pads or rotor damage. Until the brakes are inspected and repaired, avoid high-speed driving and leave extra stopping distance — if the grinding worsens, the pedal feels soft or spongy, or the vehicle pulls hard to one side under braking, have it inspected before driving further.

input.whatWentWrong: Reinigt nicht richtig, Geschirr kommt mit Essensresten heraus
input.whatTheyToldYou: Der Techniker sagte: "Die Umwälzpumpe ist defekt und muss komplett ersetzt werden"

output.understanding: Ihr etwa 4 Jahre alter Bosch-Geschirrspüler reinigt nicht richtig und ein Techniker hat eine defekte Umwälzpumpe diagnostiziert sowie deren vollständigen Austausch für €280 angeboten. Über die genaue Aufschlüsselung dieses Betrags – Teilekosten, Arbeitszeit, Anfahrt, Garantie – ist nichts Weiteres bekannt.
output.verdict_explanation: Der Gesamtbetrag von €280 wurde mündlich genannt, aber es liegt keine schriftliche Aufschlüsselung vor. Ohne zu wissen, was davon auf das Ersatzteil, was auf die Arbeitszeit und was auf eventuelle Anfahrts- oder Diagnosegebühren entfällt, lässt sich nicht beurteilen, ob der Preis angemessen ist. Außerdem ist unklar, ob eine Garantie auf die Reparatur gegeben wird und was die Diagnose konkret belegt.
unknowns_that_matter: Wie setzt sich der Betrag von €280 zusammen – Teilepreis, Arbeitszeit, Anfahrt, Diagnosegebühr?
Worauf basiert die Diagnose, dass die Umwälzpumpe defekt ist?
Gilt eine Garantie auf das Ersatzteil und/oder die Arbeit, und wenn ja, wie lange und in welchem Umfang?
Wird ein Ersatzteil verwendet, und falls ja, welches?

repair_vs_replace.assessment: Ob €280 sinnvoll sind, hängt davon ab, was ein vergleichbarer Bosch-Geschirrspüler derzeit neu kostet und in welchem sonstigen Zustand das Gerät ist. Das lässt sich aus dem vorliegenden Angebot nicht beurteilen.
missing_information: Allgemeiner Zustand und Wartungshistorie des Geräts

questions_to_ask: Können Sie mir eine schriftliche Aufschlüsselung geben, aus der Teilepreis, Arbeitszeit und etwaige Anfahrts- oder Diagnosekosten einzeln hervorgehen?
Was hat bei der Prüfung ergeben, dass die Umwälzpumpe die Ursache ist?
Welche Garantie geben Sie auf das Ersatzteil und die durchgeführte Arbeit?
Wird der Diagnosekostenanteil, falls separat berechnet, auf den Reparaturpreis angerechnet, wenn ich den Auftrag erteile?
output.what_to_say: Vielen Dank für die Einschätzung. Bevor ich den Auftrag erteile, würde ich gerne eine schriftliche Aufstellung erhalten, aus der Teilekosten, Arbeitszeit und sonstige Gebühren einzeln ersichtlich sind. Außerdem würde mich interessieren, auf welcher Grundlage die Umwälzpumpe als Ursache festgestellt wurde und welche Garantie auf Teil und Arbeit gegeben wird.

second_opinion.reason: Das Angebot liegt nur mündlich vor und ohne schriftliche Aufschlüsselung lässt sich nicht beurteilen, ob der Preis angemessen ist. Ein zweites Angebot gibt Ihnen einen Vergleich.

output.understanding: You have a 6-year-old Whirlpool refrigerator that isn't cooling properly, and ABC Appliance Repair has diagnosed a failed compressor and quoted you for a replacement. The document shows a higher total than what you typed.
output.verdict_explanation: The document clearly shows a total of $497.50, but you typed $450 as the quoted price — a $47.50 discrepancy that needs to be reconciled before you approve anything. The itemization itself is reasonably clear: parts ($310.00), labor ($187.50), and a waived service call fee ($0.00). The arithmetic on those three lines adds up correctly to $497.50, so the document is internally consistent; the issue is that the figure you were given verbally or in a different communication does not match the written invoice.

quote_summary.labor: 2.5 hours at an unstated hourly rate, totaling $187.50

document_discrepancies.document_says: Total due: $497.50 (Parts $310.00 + Labor $187.50 + Service call fee $0.00)

arithmetic_check.assessment: The three line items on the document add up exactly to the document total of $497.50 — the document is internally consistent.

specific_concerns.concern: The total on the document ($497.50) does not match the total you typed ($450.00) — a $47.50 difference.
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: You need to know which figure is the actual binding price before you authorize the work; if you were quoted $450 verbally or in writing elsewhere, you should confirm which number will appear on your final bill.

unknowns_that_matter: No warranty is stated anywhere on the document — you do not know whether the part, the labor, or the repair as a whole carries any coverage if the same problem recurs.
The compressor is listed without a part number, brand, or OEM vs. aftermarket designation — relevant if you want to compare this quote against another or verify what you are getting.
The document does not state what testing or inspection led to the compressor diagnosis — worth understanding given that this is a significant repair.

repair_vs_replace.assessment: A compressor replacement is a substantial repair cost. Without knowing the current price of a comparable replacement refrigerator, the unit's repair history, and what warranty comes with this repair, you cannot evaluate whether repairing or replacing makes more sense for your situation. A second opinion could help you weigh the decision.
missing_information: Current retail price of a comparable replacement refrigerator
Whether any warranty is included with the repair
Overall condition and repair history of this unit

questions_to_ask: The total on my invoice shows $497.50, but I had understood the quote to be $450 — can you clarify which figure is correct and what accounts for the difference?
What warranty, if any, comes with the compressor part and the labor?
Is there a warranty on the compressor part, the labor, or both — and if so, what does it cover and for how long?
Can you tell me the brand and part number of the compressor being installed, and whether it is OEM or aftermarket?
output.what_to_say: Before I approve the work, I want to sort out a discrepancy: my invoice shows a total of $497.50, but I had understood the price to be $450 — can you clarify which is correct? I also do not see any warranty listed on the document, so I would like to know what coverage, if any, comes with the part and the labor. Could you also provide the brand and part number of the compressor being installed, and let me know whether it is OEM or aftermarket?

second_opinion.reason: A compressor replacement is one of the more substantial refrigerator repairs, the diagnosis is not documented on the quote, and there is a price discrepancy to resolve — a second opinion could independently confirm the diagnosis and give you a comparable price to check scope and cost.

output.understanding: You have a written estimate from Metro Auto Repair for a 2018 Honda Civic with a grinding noise when braking. The quote covers a full brake job on all four corners — pads, rotors, and calipers — totaling $1,708.00.
output.verdict_explanation: The quote is clearly itemized and the arithmetic checks out, so you can see exactly what you are being asked to pay for. Before approving, it is worth understanding the inspection findings that led to recommending all four calipers ($660.00 of the total) in addition to pads and rotors — the estimate does not detail what was observed. Getting that detail would let you evaluate whether the full scope fits what was found.

quote_summary.stated_diagnosis: Grinding noise when braking (symptom only — no documented finding or caliper condition stated in the estimate)
quote_summary.proposed_work: Replace front brake pads, front brake rotors (2), rear brake pads, rear brake rotors (2), front calipers (2), and rear calipers (2)

arithmetic_check.assessment: All seven line items sum to exactly $1,708.00, matching the stated total — no arithmetic discrepancy.

specific_concerns.concern: The 24-hour approval deadline is printed on the estimate itself.
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: Pressure to decide quickly on a $1,708.00 repair limits your ability to ask follow-up questions, get a second opinion, or simply think it over — and a reputable shop can generally hold a price beyond an arbitrary window if asked.

unknowns_that_matter: Whether the inspection findings that led to recommending all four calipers are documented anywhere — the estimate lists the symptom and the proposed work but does not detail what was observed during the inspection.
Whether the parts are OEM, OEM-equivalent, or aftermarket, and whether they carry any parts warranty — neither is stated in the estimate.
Whether any labor warranty or guarantee on the completed work is offered — the estimate is silent on this.
Whether tax is included in the $1,708.00 total or would be added at invoice.
questions_to_ask: What did the inspection find on the calipers that led to the recommendation to replace all four?
Do the parts and labor carry any warranty, and if so, for how long?
Is tax included in the $1,708.00 estimate, or will that be added at the end?
Can you hold this price for a few days while I review the estimate — I want to make sure I understand everything before I approve.
output.what_to_say: Thank you for the written estimate. Before I approve, I have a few questions. I would like to understand what was found during the inspection that indicates all four calipers need replacing in addition to the pads and rotors — can you walk me through what you observed? I also want to confirm whether parts and labor carry any warranty, and whether tax is included in the $1,708.00 total. I need a couple of days to review this, so I would appreciate you holding the price while I do that.

second_opinion.reason: Replacing all four calipers is a significant portion of this estimate ($660.00). Getting a second inspection would give you independent confirmation of the findings and let you compare the recommended scope before committing.

output.safety_note: Grinding when braking can indicate worn brake components. If braking feels significantly reduced, the pedal feels soft or spongy, or the vehicle pulls hard to one side under braking, limit driving and have the brakes inspected promptly — do not wait on the written estimate process in that case.
